name: fachan

attributes.attribute: haunted the wilder districts of Scotland
held a flail covered with iron apples
struck passersby while hopping on one leg
cast curses on one leg with an arm raised

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The fachan, also called the athach, is a Scottish folkloric figure. It is a one-legged, one-eyed monster of Scotland's wild country. A single hand grew from its chest. That hand gripped a flail thick with iron apples. It struck at passersby while hopping on its one leg. The creature came in two forms, the first being the Athach. The other form, the dìreach, prowled the quiet Glen Eitive. A druid would curse by balancing on one leg and lifting an arm. Some believe the fachan stories grew from fear of that posture. The posture is linked to the Glám Dícenn.

okr.objective: The fachan is a one-legged, one-eyed monster of the Scottish wilds.
